title: Runner operation
description: A typed code-execution operation submitted to a runner (PRD §13.7), kept runner-neutral so both the headspace Docker runner and a Lambda container-image function adapter map onto the same document. The control plane never executes code: it describes an operation, and a runner executes it behind an enforced policy boundary. A wrapper that checks policy and then hands an unrestricted shell to another process does not satisfy that boundary.

operation_id.description: Caller-assigned operation identity, also the idempotency key for dispatch.

runner.description: Logical runner name, e.g. `headspace` or `lambda`. The engine does not branch on this value; adapters register under it.

runner_revision.description: Pinned revision of the runner the caller expects. Part of the replay manifest.

workspace.description: Immutable input workspace. Absent when the operation genuinely has no workspace — absence is explicit, never an empty stand-in.

source_ref.description: Artifact reference for the input workspace, e.g. `artifact://workspace/input`.

write_mode.description: `copy-on-write` is the safe default; inputs stay immutable either way.

execution.description: The pinned execution environment. `container` covers an OCI image run by an isolating runner; `function` covers a managed function backed by a container image. Both are pinned by image digest — an unpinned tag is not an execution environment.

image_ref.description: Registry reference or registered function identity. Dispatch to an identity absent from the runner's registry is refused by the adapter, not by this schema.

user.description: Non-root execution identity, e.g. `65532:65532`, when the runner can set one.

read_only_root.description: Read-only root filesystem. Safe default is true.

command.description: What to execute inside the pinned image. The command is an argument array, never a shell string.

environment_refs.description: Named references to individually granted environment values. No implicit environment is inherited and secrets are absent unless granted.

requires_shell.description: Declared explicitly when a shell is genuinely required, so policy can reject the operation instead of discovering the shell at runtime.

policy.description: Limits enforced inside dispatch to the runner. Fields a given runner cannot enforce must be rejected by that adapter rather than silently ignored.

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock bound. An adapter whose platform caps duration below this value rejects the operation at validate time, naming the cap.

cpu.description: CPU units. Omitted when the runner derives CPU from memory rather than accepting it.

egress_allowlist.description: Required to be meaningful only when `network` is `egress-allowlist`.

allowed_output_paths.description: Explicitly allowed output paths. An empty array means no writable output is permitted, and says so.

evidence.description: What the caller asks the runner to observe. A runner that cannot honour a request must say so in the result's observations rather than fabricate the observation.

context.description: Optional correlation back to the graph: run, node run, and attempt. The runner treats these as opaque.
